limitations: Public Bitcoin witness/input verification and signed checker evidence do not independently verify RGB consignments; receiver-owned SDK/indexer supplies asset/receive membership.
Public test-only flagged list is synthetic policy data; this proves exact actual witness-input matching, not Utexo production flagged-list integration.
Snapshot rollback detection assumes a current trusted retained local journal/checkpoint. Rolling back snapshot, journal and checkpoint together needs an external anchor, which is not built.
Direct raw wallet keys/SDK signing calls lie outside the governed adapter boundary; signatures already exported cannot be revoked.
Ambiguous crash state fails closed and requires reviewed offline recovery. Daily limits conservatively retain failed-send reservations until UTC-day rollover.

Signed logs bind receipt action/token/plan/policy hashes. The compact public receipt does not disclose a full prepared PSBT; native exact-transaction handling is covered by source audit and independent probes.
